title: Thermal cascade optimization of PCM‐integrated hollow bricks for enhanced dynamic thermal inertia in hot semi‐arid climates
content:
Abstract

The increasing demand for cooling in hot and semi-arid areas underscores the need for passive building-envelope solutions that reduce heat gains and improve indoor thermal stability. This work investigates the transient thermal performance of a hollow brick containing phase change materials under severe summer conditions in Gabès, Tunisia. A two-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was developed using ANSYS Fluent R19.0 and validated against experimental data from the literature using the enthalpy-porosity method, with a maximum relative error of less than 3%. Five consecutive days were simulated with four PCM configurations using a fixed RT26 internal layer and different external PCMs, namely RT26, RT28, RT31, and RT35, separated by a central air cavity. The results demonstrate that PCM performance is strongly dependent on the melting temperature and nighttime regeneration capacity. The RT26-Air-RT26 configuration reaches thermal saturation after the second cycle and increases the indoor heat flux in the following days, highlighting the risk of using low-melting-temperature PCMs in hot climates. Ultimately, the RT35-Air-RT26 setup emerged as the optimal configuration for thermal regulation. Compared to the air-filled reference case, this optimal configuration reduced the peak indoor heat flux by 29.9%, decreased the decrement factor by 80.7%, dampened the indoor temperature amplitude by 71.8%, lowered the peak inner-surface temperature by 0.92°C (3.16%), and introduced a thermal time lag of 1.25 h. The study demonstrates that a graded strategy, combining a high-melting-temperature external PCM with a lower-melting-temperature internal PCM, effectively improves the dynamic thermal inertia of building envelopes.
